sections.h2: How soon can a Mission house be sold?
sections.html: Within weeks if you choose cash. Buyers there include investors and out-of-town heirs' purchasers, and sellers often pick cash after inheriting a house, leaving the Valley or facing repairs. Have your deed and tax bill ready.

sections.h2: What is Mission, Texas known for?
sections.html:
Mission is a Hidalgo County city on the Rio Grande, founded in 1908 when the Missouri Pacific Railroad set up a station near the center of a new development. It was named for La Lomita Chapel, and the city's history page says the population is approaching 70,000.

The city describes this area as the place where citrus was first planted in the Rio Grande Valley. The multimillion-dollar citrus industry is celebrated each year at the Texas Citrus Fiesta, each year. For a seller, that heritage is the backdrop to the local housing stock.

  • The historic La Lomita Mission still stands and draws visitors.
  • William Jennings Bryan built a winter home in Mission, and the area appears in Larry McMurtry's Lonesome Dove.
  • Land here began as Spanish porciones that ran about two-thirds of a mile along the river and 11 to 16 miles inland, a pattern recorded in county land records.

sections.h2: Which sale routes does a Mission owner have?
sections.html:
Three paths, each with its own timing.

  • Cash buyer. Suits as-is sales, clouded inherited title and storm or roof damage.
  • Agent listing. Can bring more for homes in good shape, with showings and financing timelines.
  • Seller financing. Slower and regulated: a contract for deed on a residence falls under Property Code chapter 5, and the buyer holds a right to cancel.

Get every offer in writing and learn who covers title, recording and survey.

sections.h2: What does Mission's history mean for property records?
sections.html:
Land around Mission began as Spanish porciones, long strips of land along the river. The city's history notes that porciones 55 and 57 held Rancho La Lomita, home of the chapel for which the city is named. Later the Rancho La Lomita Land Company, run by Captain Conway and J.W. Hoit, developed the area, and the railroad station of 1908 anchored the new town.

That history is why older Mission parcels can carry long chains of ownership in county records. A title search follows each link. If your family has held the land for generations, collect any old deeds, family agreements or probate papers you have, because gaps in the chain can slow a sale. A cash buyer's title company can tell you early what it needs.

sections.h2: What does Mission require for building permits and repairs?
sections.html:
Mission's Inspections Division reviews permits for new buildings and checks compliance with minimum building codes. A permit is also required for any concrete or asphalt slab with a value of $100 or more, and mobile homes need permits.

Inspectors check foundation, plumbing, framing, mechanical, A/C, electrical, setbacks, sidewalks and buffering on new residences. Structures that existed before annexation are treated as grandfathered while they stay as they are, but expanding one requires a permit and brings zoning and setback rules into play. The division's phone is 956-580-8691 per the city page. Before you list, ask whether an addition, slab or carport was permitted, since open work can slow a buyer's lender.

sections.h2: How does the appraisal district affect a Mission sale?
sections.html:
Hidalgo CAD values Mission property and takes homestead and over-65 applications through an online portal. Its customer service line is 956-381-8466.

Statewide, homestead notices arrive near April 1, and the usual protest cutoff is mid-May. State law caps annual growth in a homestead's appraised value at 10 percent. Ask the district which exemptions are on your account so you can tell a buyer what to expect after closing. The district's official site lists the portal and contact details.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can a Mission buyer apply for?
sections.html:
A buyer who will occupy the home can file for a residence homestead exemption. School districts give $140,000, with $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled.

  • Someone buying after January 1 may receive it immediately for that year when you never claimed it.
  • Disabled veterans get $5,000 to $12,000 by rating, and a 100 percent rating can cover the whole homestead.
  • Heirs missing from the deed can apply with an ownership affidavit, a death certificate and a utility bill.

See the Comptroller exemptions page.

sections.h2: What if unpaid taxes lead to a tax sale?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes become a lien that can be foreclosed. The Comptroller says a lien attaches every January 1 and lets a court seize property even if ownership has changed. Collectors can add court costs, and private attorneys under contract can add up to 20 percent.

If land was sold at a tax sale, redemption rights are narrow. For a homestead, the owner has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed, paying a premium of 25 percent in the first year or 50 percent in the second, plus costs. Other property has 180 days. Former owners have two years to claim excess proceeds. Request a payoff and itemized statement from the tax office before deciding.

  • Over-65 or disabled homeowners may pay delinquent amounts in installments.
  • Some collectors allow plans of up to 36 months, required on a homestead.
  • A waiver of penalty and interest must be asked for in writing.

sections.h2: How does a Mission seller compare offers?
sections.html:
Line up each offer on the same terms. A high price with a long inspection period can net you less than a lower cash offer that closes promptly.

  • Price and whether it is as-is.
  • Closing date and who selects the title company.
  • Who pays title, recording and survey fees.
  • Earnest money and what happens to it if the buyer backs out.
  • Whether the buyer needs financing or an appraisal.

Ask for the final numbers on a closing statement. If anything looks unclear, ask the title company, not the buyer, to explain it.

sections.h2: How do liens, probate and foreclosure play out in Mission?
sections.html:
Liens and taxes come out of proceeds at closing. For an inherited house, expect the title company to ask for orders or recorded papers naming who may sign. Wills must be probated within four years of death.

A lender usually forecloses by nonjudicial auction on a first Tuesday, with notice 21 days ahead. A deficiency suit must follow within two years. Selling first keeps equity with you. The State Law Library foreclosure guide explains the stages.

sections.h2: Where is a Mission deed recorded?
sections.html: With the clerk of the county where the land lies, after notarized signature. The 2023 clerk manual lists $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages plus capped records fees. Verify the current figures with the clerk.

sections.h2: What should I ask a buyer before signing in Mission?
sections.html: Ask who the purchaser is, whether the offer is as-is, and where earnest money sits. Ask what closing date they propose and what happens if a title problem appears. Read the contract in full before signing, and make sure the title company, not the buyer, prepares your closing statement.

faqs.q: Is a storm-damaged Mission house sellable?
faqs.a: Yes, to cash buyers who price in the repairs. Listing usually means fixing damage for lender approval.

faqs.q: When does Mission require a permit for concrete?
faqs.a: For any slab worth $100 or more. Expanding an older structure also needs a permit and brings zoning setbacks into play.

faqs.q: Who sets appraised values in Mission?
faqs.a: The Hidalgo County Appraisal District. Reach customer service at 956-381-8466 or use its portal for homestead and over-65 filings.

faqs.q: What proves I can sell an inherited house?
faqs.a: A muniment of title, administration or a transfer on death deed. A will must be probated within four years of death.
If closing happens before the auction, yes. Texas allows 20 days to reinstate after the default notice and at least 21 days' notice of sale.
